flags: Published prose claiming the valley is kept out of sight is unsupported and removed. The cache says the Commercial Club commissioned a Viking statue in 1972, not that it installed it on Pyramid Hill that year; that claim is removed.

Tourism and Wikipedia give different exact Hi-Line construction start dates (June 30 versus July 5, 1906). Their May 1908 dates refer to readiness, an official crossing and regular service; the story uses only the shared year.
The cache lacks a named Indigenous community source for the footpath history and Pyramid Hill traditions. No specific nation or sacred-site interpretation is inferred.
Lisbon is deliberately short: the cache provides little relevant town narrative beyond its naming and theater. No continuous-operation superlative or current visitor arrangements are asserted.
The cache describes a 63-mile byway, while material maps 77.5 miles. Public copy uses the cache figure.
